scope.method: Independent Standards and Spec source reviews, root review of queue/retry/report/CLI and contract boundaries, focused existing tests and passive reproductions. No checkout switch or source repair.

standards.conclusion: No additional actionable documented-standard violations. Identifier and FPS compatibility defects are counted once each on the Spec axis.

findings.title: Validate generated composition identifiers before native capture
findings.trigger: Set an otherwise valid native plan speech ID to cue.main, or to 122 alphabetic characters.
findings.actual: The public native plan schema and compiler accept the ID. composeBlenderEpisode prefixes it with speech-/panel- and then CompositionSchema rejects the generated layer IDs: punctuation violates compositionId's regex and the speech prefix makes the long ID exceed its 128-character bound.
findings.impact: The production executor performs prepareBlenderEpisodePlates before composing the receiving document, so these admitted plans can consume a complete native capture and then deterministically fail export. Callout IDs and numeric-leading plan IDs have analogous composition-ID boundaries. A 201-character shot ID also passes compilation/composition but fails the mandatory quality-policy shot bound.
findings.recommendation: Use compatible contracts or deterministic bounded IDs for generated composition identifiers, preserve native object/camera/anchor names separately, and validate the receiving composition and quality-policy structure during preflight.

findings.title: Restrict native episode FPS to the receiving composition limit

specification.quote: Capability discovery and generated docs must agree on import, batch and preview/export limits.

findings.trigger: Use 120 FPS in a valid two-second native episode with 240 frames and a matching complete shot partition.
findings.actual: BlenderEpisodePlanSchema, compileBlenderEpisode, planBlenderProductionReview and admitBlenderProductionVisualWork pass. composeBlenderEpisode rejects fps because CompositionFpsSchema permits at most 60 FPS.
findings.impact: All native episode rates 61-120 are advertised and admitted despite being impossible to export through the required receiving composition. The executor reaches this rejection after native capture.
findings.recommendation: Bind native episode FPS to CompositionFpsSchema or reject unsupported episode export rates before capture. Raw Blender capture may retain its independent 120-FPS limit.

limits: Focused verification only; no fresh full check:fast, check:runtime, release gate, full render matrix or all-ten installed production run.
Identifier/FPS reproductions are passive compiler/contract checks and perform no Blender capture or media generation.
No continuous playback, listening, encoded-glyph review or human/product acceptance is inferred.
Existing acceptance gaps, failed pilot targets and unavailable token measurements are explicitly disclosed by the PR and are not counted as hidden implementation defects.
No GitHub review comments, fixes, commits, pushes or merges were performed. Findings are delivered in this chat and local records.
